name: How to Prepare Your Property for a Fencing Contractor in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: How should I prepare my Los Angeles County property before a fencing contractor arrives to keep costs from creeping up?
mainEntity.text: How should I prepare my Los Angeles County property before a fencing contractor arrives to keep costs from creeping up?

acceptedAnswer.text: Unexpected site-prep can quietly increase fence costs if it is not discussed beforehand. A few days before your Los Angeles County fencing contractor arrives, walk the proposed fence line and remove loose items like furniture, planters, toys, and yard clutter that could block access. Clear manageable vegetation such as low shrubs, vines, and tall grass if you agreed to handle that yourself; heavy brush or tree removal is usually extra and should be quoted separately. Pick up pet waste and secure animals indoors or in another part of the yard during working hours. Mark known underground features—sprinkler lines, landscape lighting, drains—and provide the contractor with any site plans you have. Ask whether they will call utility marking services for gas, electric, and communication lines or if that falls on you. Clarify access points, such as gates or shared driveways, so crews can bring in materials and tools without delays. Before work begins, confirm in writing which prep tasks are included in the contract and which will result in change orders. Proper preparation reduces labor time, avoids damage to your belongings and utilities, and helps keep the project on schedule and on budget.
acceptedAnswer.description: Before fence installation, clear vegetation, movable items, and pet waste along the fence line and mark any underground utilities. Ask your Los Angeles County fencing contractor what they expect you to handle versus what they will bill as extra site-prep work.
